newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.

text.p: Australian Meat and Livestock Corp's (AMLC) weekly export prices are as follows:
AUSTRALIAN EXPORT PRICES TO U.S. IN U.S. CENTS/LB, CIF.
Bull (95 Chemical Lean) 82 -1 on last week
AUSTRALIAN EXPORT PRICES TO JAPAN IN U.S. CENTS/LB CIF.
Chilled grassfed fullsets 146 +9 on last week
AMLC COMMENTARY: Cattle prices were mildy positive this week, with the exception of southern Australia.
The major news of the week was good news for cattle producers.
In addition to welcome rain in Queensland, the Northern Territory, New South Wales and Western Australia, prices for chilled beef to Australia's major export market lifted sharply.
The rise in export prices reflects a jump in wholesale prices in Japan.
The latest price increase seems to be due to three factors -- better than expected end of year demand, tight supplies from Australia and reduced expectations of U.S. supplies in early January.
Prices on the U.S. imported grinding beef market were mixed to slightly higher, in spite of a falling domestic market because of limited Australian and New Zealand offerings.
Demand for imported product is reported as very light, in part the result of weakening prices in the domestic lean beef market as well as a slowdown in business related to the Christmas break.
Australian lean grinding beef prices finished the week moderately higher.
Imported trimmings also rose in price this week, on limited offerings and higher prices for equivalent domestic product.
